dataset: India Flood Inventory v3.0 - filter to Mumbai/Maharashtra events (incl. 26 July 2005)
source: India Flood Inventory v3 project, republished via bharatlas (urbanmorph/geodata)
download_date: NOT YET DOWNLOADED (28.6 MB geojson, national coverage - download once then filter to Maharashtra/Mumbai locally, do not attempt to pull through chat context)
format: GeoJSON (national, 1,006 flood event polygons, 1960s-2020); also Parquet 5.3MB, PMTiles, KML, Shapefile
spatial_resolution: event-level polygons, resolution varies by event/source
coverage: Pan-India; MUST BE FILTERED locally (e.g. by state='Maharashtra' or bbox clip to Mumbai) after download
quality: medium-high (compiled catalogue; source quality varies by event/era)
limitations: National dataset requiring local filtering; event polygon precision for older events (like 2005) may be coarse.
processing: NONE performed here; filtering to Mumbai must happen after download using scripts/filter_flood_inventory.py

dataset: NDEM All-India Flood Inundation 1998-2022 - filter to Mumbai
download_date: NOT YET DOWNLOADED (87.3 MB geojson, national - filter locally)
coverage: Pan-India satellite-derived flood inundation extents 1998-2022; filter to Mumbai bbox after download
limitations: Satellite-derived inundation extents, not point-level 'flood observations' with depth/timing detail.
notes: Good complement to India Flood Inventory for spatial extent of major events.

dataset: 26 July 2005 Mumbai flood - narrative/secondary reporting (NOT precise geospatial ground truth)
source: Multiple: Wikipedia 'Maharashtra floods of 2005', Govt of Maharashtra Fact Finding Committee report (2006), NIDM Journal (nidm.gov.in), arxiv.org/abs/2306.09770 (academic crowdsourced-data study)
license: varies by source (Wikipedia CC-BY-SA; academic papers per their own terms - check before redistribution)
download_date: web pages identified 2026-09-23, not archived as structured data here
format: narrative text / figures in PDF reports (Fact Finding Committee 2006 has inundation extent FIGURES, not machine-readable GIS)
coverage: 26-27 July 2005 event; Santacruz station recorded 944mm/24hr, Colaba 73-84mm/24hr (station values vary slightly by source - verify against IMD primary records before using)
quality: low as geospatial ground truth - these are narrative/report sources per task instructions ('do NOT treat news articles as precise geospatial ground truth')
limitations: No machine-readable point/polygon flood-extent file with lat/lon and water depth was found for this event beyond the two catalogue datasets above.
notes: Use as context/validation narrative, not as primary GIS input. The Fact Finding Committee report's Figures 7-8 (inundated areas) would need manual georeferencing if used.
